title: Generation of Heterogeneous Drug Gradients Across Cancer Populations on a Microfluidic Evolution Accelerator for Real-Time Observation
protocol: Generate the desired microfluidic pattern using layout design software.
Fabricate the photomask.
Write the pattern on a soda-lime glass plate coated with 100 nm of Cr and 500 nm of photoresist AZ1518 using a laser writer.
Develop the photoresist with developer AZ300MIF for 60 seconds.
Etch away the chromium without protection from the photoresist using Cr-7 Chromium Etchant.
Strip off residual photoresist using a photoresist stripper at 70 °C for 45 minutes.
Spin coat HMDS on silicon wafer at 4000 rpm for 40 seconds.
Spin coat photoresist AZ4330 on silicon wafer at 4000 rpm for 40 seconds.
Soft bake the silicon wafer at 95 °C for 60 seconds.
Expose UV to the silicon wafer using a mask aligner.
Develop the photoresist with developer AZ300MIF for 4 minutes.
Perform DRIE etching on the wafer patterned with the photoresist using a Silicon Deep Reactive Ion Etching (DRIE) system for 100 µm depth.
Dry-etch the wafer patterned with the photoresist using an acetone solution and plasma etch with a plasma etcher to strip off the photoresist.
Perform thermal oxidation on the etched silicon wafer in a furnace at 1100 °C for 1 hour.
Wait for the silicon wafer to cool down.
Place the cooled silicon wafer into a desiccator.
Drip several drops of trichloro-1H,1H,2H,2H-perfluorooctyl-silane (PFOTS) in a small container near the wafer.
Pump the pressure of the desiccator to 0.5 atm at room temperature for 60 min.
Mix pre-polymer and cross-linker from polymethylsiloxane (PDMS) kit at a 10:1 by weight ratio.
Pour the mixed PDMS to create a 10 mm film in height onto the silanized silicon wafer mold.
Degas the resulting PDMS-silicon wafer system in a desiccator for 30 min to 1 h.
Incubate the PDMS-silicon wafer in a 70 °C incubator overnight to cure the PDMS.
Peel the cured PDMS film off the silicon wafer carefully.
Punch through-holes at the inlet ports on the PDMS using biopsy needles based on the pattern location.
Cut chips 27 mm in diameter from the PDMS layer using a circular punch.
Heat cure two stacks of 27 mm PDMS cylinders for the reservoir layer and capping layer.
Cut out two 7 mm circles around the inlets on the reservoir layer.
Punch through-holes at the inlet ports on the capping layer using a biopsy needle.
Bond three stacks of PDMS (patterned stack, reservoir layer, capping layer) with oxygen plasma treatment.
Punch through-holes at the outlets and the center port of the device using a biopsy needle.
Prepare media for culturing PC3 cell lines by mixing RPMI 1640 medium with 10% fetal bovine serum (FBS) and 1x antibiotic-antimycotic.
Generate cell lines as described previously.
Maintain PC3 cell lines in humidified incubators at 37 °C with 5% CO2.
Split cells and subculture every 3 days before they reach 100% confluency.
Transfect PC3-EMT cell line with cytoplasmic GFP for better visualization.
Transfect PC3-EPI cell line with cytoplasmic mCherry for better visualization.
Fabricate a plate holder sufficient to hold simultaneous gas-permeable culture dishes by machining or 3D printing.
Unscrew the components of the holder using a screwdriver.
Disinfect the components via UV exposure for at least 1 h.
Harvest PC3-EPI and PC3-EMT cells by trypsinization for 5 min.
Add prewarmed culture media, then centrifuge at 150 x g for 3 min and discard the supernatant.
Count cells of each PC3-EPI and PC3-EMT using a hemocytometer.
Isolate a total of 2.5 x 10^4 of each cell type for each gas-permeable culture dish.
Mix and resuspend the two cell types in 2 ml of culture media.
Seed the cells into each of the gas-permeable culture dishes.
Leave the entire plate holder in the incubator overnight for cells to attach.
Disinfect PDMS devices via UV exposure for at least 1 h.
Set up a gas supply system consisting of CO2 and O2 control units, a gas pump, a gas mixing chamber, a humidifier or bubbler, and three separate sets of gas valves and pressure gauges.
Set up CO2 and O2 control units to adjust gas mixing rates from CO2, N2 tanks, and an O2 source.
Combine the gases in a mixing chamber and humidify by a bubbler to achieve 85% relative humidity.
Connect the gas to three independent valves with pressure gauges for controlling flow rate.
Place the plate holder in an on-stage incubation thermal control unit set at 37 °C.
Install the microfluidic device.
Identify that the detailed components of the 3-well plate holder are in order.
Pre-warm culture medium at 37 °C and degas in a vacuum chamber for 20 min.
Treat the PDMS chips using an oxygen plasma system for 30 s to maintain hydrophilicity.
Set up the syringe system.
Load two syringes slowly with growth media.
Load other two syringes with desired reagent of interest (media, media with drug, etc.).
Connect each individual syringe to a 50 cm tubing by a 23 G dispensing needle into one hollow steel pin.
Insert the other end of the tubing into a hollow steel pin.
Prime the tubing and insert the steel pin into each PDMS chip through the capping layer.
Fill up the reservoir layer and wet the PDMS pattern layer with media.
Load a 1 mL syringe with culture media.
Connect the syringe to a 5 cm tubing (0.020" x 0.060"OD) by a 23 G dispensing needle into one hollow steel pin.
Insert a hollow steel pin into the other end of the tubing and prime the tubing.
Insert the hollow steel pin into the center hole of the chip, where excessive media can be extracted out from the chip later during the chip sealing process.
Load two 10 mL syringes per chip in the forward deck.
Place the two other syringes in the withdraw deck of the syringe system.
Place chip directly on top of the gas-permeable culture membranes (with cells already adhered to the membranes).
Dispense 1 mL of prewarmed and degassed media into the 35 mm gas-permeable culture dish before assembly.
Approach the liquid surface with a 15-degree tilt angle when placing the chip on top of the culture membrane.
Clamp the gas-permeable culture dish and the well in the gas-permeable culture dish holder for each chip, with the PDMS chip holder pushing the PDMS device downward.
Tape a sheet of a sealer on top of the PDMS device and clamp with the PDMS chip holder to prevent the chip from drying out.
Set media flow rate around the array to be 20 µL/h.
Set the entire plate in the on-stage incubator on the motorized stage of an inverted microscope.
Connect the gas supply system to the gas channels and pressurize the gas-permeable culture membrane against the installed PDMS chip to ensure sealing of the device.
Maintain gauge pressure at 0.2 psi (1.4 x 10^4 Pa).
Slowly extract excessive media in the chip using the 1-mL syringe from the center hole.
Observe the chip under the microscope while extracting media and stop when the chip is sealed.
Connect the temperature sensing unit of the on-stage incubator to the 3-well plate and set it to 37 °C.
Set up imaging software utilizing an inverted microscope for time-lapse image acquisition.
Configure software to acquire images across two channels at 10x magnification for each chip with automatic image-stitching after one round of autofocus.
Take images every hour.
Monitor image quality on a daily basis.
Update the focus surface as necessary.
Prepare the PDMS chip for immunofluorescent analysis.
Prepare the gas-permeable culture dish for immunofluorescent analysis.
Convert images into TIFF format using Fiji/ImageJ.
Compress TIFF files for further processing.
Perform Background Subtraction to identify cells.
Perform Particle Analysis to detect fluorescent bright-spots.
Use plugins such as Manual Tracking, Chemotaxis, Migration Tool, and Trackmate for cell motility and migration analysis.
